title: Random Forests — Reduce Variance by Weakening Agreement
key_insight: Bootstrap rows and random feature subsets reduce correlation between trees. The forest mainly lowers variance—the sensitivity of one deep tree to its training sample.
body:
## Reduce Variance by Weakening Agreement

Averaging helps most when models are individually useful but do not make the same errors. Perfectly matching trees gain nothing from a vote.

Bootstrap rows and random feature subsets reduce correlation between trees. The forest mainly lowers variance—the sensitivity of one deep tree to its training sample.

Parallel training is easy because trees are independent, but serving many large trees can stress memory caches. Compress, limit depth, or distill when latency matters.
common_mistakes: Assuming more trees repair biased or bad data.
Trusting split importance as unbiased evidence.
Ignoring prediction cost when serving a very large forest.
